3. Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Protection & Anonymization
Under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP) and corporate privacy standards, all datasets used in analytics, model training, or QA testing must undergo cryptographic tokenization or masking:
Masking Protocols: Phone numbers, email handles, and national identifiers (Aadhaar, PAN) must be SHA-256 hashed or dynamic-masked.
Synthetic Data Generation: Analytics pipelines in non-production environments must utilize synthetic data generated via approved scripts.
Data Retention & Purging: Temporary staging tables containing sensitive raw extracts must automatically purge after 14 calendar days.
Note: Statutory position to be verified by qualified legal/HR counsel before real-world use.

heading_path: Engineering Development Workflow, Git & Code Review Guide > 2. Git Repository & Branching Strategy

2. Git Repository & Branching Strategy
Northstar uses enterprise GitLab (gitlab.northstar.example) for source code hosting. Teams follow a standardized Git branching model:
main / production: Represents production-ready code. Direct commits and force pushes are strictly disabled. Changes enter solely via merged pull/merge requests.
release/*: Release staging branches for final system testing, QA sign-off, and hotfix stabilization before scheduled deployment.
develop: Active development branch for integrated feature testing across sprint iterations.
feature/*: Individual feature work branches created from develop. Named according to convention: feature/JIRA-123-short-description.
hotfix/*: Urgent production patch branches branched directly from main, requiring expedited manager approval.

heading_path: Engineering Development Workflow, Git & Code Review Guide > 3. Merge Request (MR) & Code Review Protocol

3. Merge Request (MR) & Code Review Protocol
High software quality and security require rigorous peer review. Every Merge Request must meet these criteria before merging:
Peer Review Approval: At least one mandatory approving review from a designated senior engineer (Vikram Joshi EMP-007, Mira Nair EMP-008, or Engineering Manager Ananya Iyer EMP-006).
Automated CI Validation: All automated pipeline checks (unit tests, static linting, security scans) must pass completely with green status.
Test Coverage Threshold: Code changes must demonstrate at least 80% automated test coverage for new business logic.
No Sensitive Credentials: Zero embedded secrets, API keys, or plaintext connection strings (verified via pre-commit trufflehog/gitleaks scan).
Commit Standards: Clear, conventional commit messages referencing active Jira issue tickets (e.g., 'feat(auth): add MFA session validation #NST-452').

ACCESS RESTRICTION: This section is classified FINANCE_ONLY. Only members of the Finance & Administration department (GRP_DEPT_FIN) may access this content.

Q: Is the 15-minute grace period cumulative?
A: No. The grace period applies per day. However, if you are consistently late (more than 3 times in a month), the pattern will be flagged.

All work must be conducted on company-provisioned laptops managed by IT. Employees must not disable endpoint antivirus, firewall, or MDM profiles.

5. Data Classification Framework
All company and customer data must be classified into one of four tiers:
Tier 1: Public: Marketing materials, publicly released software documentation, website content. No special safeguards.
Tier 2: Internal: Internal policies, employee handbook, general company announcements, directory. Standard employee access.
Tier 3: Confidential: Source code, customer project deliverables, contracts, financial reports, operational architecture. Role-based access.
Tier 4: Restricted: Customer PII, production credentials, private cryptographic keys, HR disciplinary files, fraud investigation records. Strictly segregated access with audit logging.

7. Security Incident Response Procedures — Internal Playbook
ACCESS RESTRICTION: This section is classified IT_ONLY. Only members of the Information Technology department (GRP_DEPT_IT) may access this content.
7.1 Incident Containment and Network Isolation
Upon confirmation of a Severity P1 or P2 incident, IT engineers must execute containment within 30 minutes:
Network Isolation: Remotely disconnect the infected endpoint from corporate Wi-Fi/VPN via MDM console without powering off.
Session Revocation: Invalidate active OAuth tokens and terminate Google Workspace, GitLab, and VPN sessions for compromised accounts.
Firewall Rule Enforcement: Block identified malicious external IP addresses and domains at the perimeter gateway.
7.2 Forensic Evidence Preservation
Volatile memory (RAM) must be imaged prior to system reboot using approved forensic tooling. Disk drive BitLocker recovery keys must be secured, and chain-of-custody documentation logged in Jira Service Desk under the CONFIDENTIAL-SEC project.
7.3 Breach Notification Decision Criteria
Statutory and customer breach notification triggers are evaluated exclusively by the IT Manager (Neha Kulkarni) and CEO (Aarav Mehta). Under applicable Indian data protection frameworks, notification protocols must initiate within prescribed statutory windows following incident confirmation.
Note: Statutory position to be verified by qualified legal/HR counsel before real-world use.

Q: How often must I change my password?
A: Passwords expire every 90 days. You will receive an automated prompt 7 days prior to expiry.
Q: Can I plug in a personal USB drive to copy files?
A: No. USB storage devices are blocked by default. Request an IT exception if business-essential.
Q: What is the screen lock timeout?
A: Screens lock automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity.
